pr_body:
This PR adds support for long read for both the unicast client and server. 

To use the long read procedure, the code had to be changed to use read by handle, instead of read by UUID. Furthermore, read by UUID isn't mandatory to support in BAP, and have caused issues during UPF, so that change is a win-win. 

This also adds support for long writes in ASCS (mandatory to support), but the effort to support long writes by the client takes more effort (and is not mandatory to support), so that has been offloaded to https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/54367

fixes https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/53159
closes https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/50796

issue_context.title: LE Audio: Add BAP Read Long procedure
issue_context.body:
**Is your enhancement proposal related to a problem? Please describe.**
The BAP Unicast Server may have PAC records (and even ASE states) that exceeds the minimum required MTU of 65. In those cases the Unicast Server should support the Read Long procedure. 

The current BAP Unicast Client does not support the Read Long procedure, but to support devices with many or large PAC records, it should. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Implement support for the Read Long procedure in the BAP Unicast Client. This requires adding a buffer for the unicast client to store partial data until the entire characteristic has been read. The size of the buffer should match the maximum length of data we otherwise support (but maximum 512 (`BT_ATT_MAX_ATTRIBUTE_LEN`). 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
N/A

**Additional context**
See e.g. the tbs_client.c implementation for an already existing implementation of this.

Do we need 2 empty lines here or one will be enough?
if there is more to discover, should it not return BT_GATT_ITER_CONTINUE?

We could do that, yes. 

So in the case of 3 ASEs, where we want to discover and read them all, we can either do 

Option A):
1) Discover ASE_1
2) Discover ASE_2
3) Discover ASE_3
4) Read ASE_1
5) Read ASE_2
6) Read ASE_3

or 

Option B):
1) Discover ASE_1
2) Read ASE_1
3) Discover ASE_2
4) Read ASE_2
5) Discover ASE_3
6) Read ASE_3

Either way requires 6 GATT requests, so the order does not really matter that much, and we are currently using Option B.
If we have similar patterns other places in the host code, we should probably stick with that (pattern).
